subject: Meteorology
title: Energy Balance at the Surface
description: A fast breakdown of Energy Balance at the Surface for builders.

hook.text: Earth's surface gains and loses energy constantly—if the budget doesn't balance, temperatures change.

buildup.text: Incoming solar radiation minus reflected energy, plus downward longwave from the atmosphere, equals net input.

discovery.text: The surface loses energy through longwave emission, sensible heat flux, latent heat flux, and ground heat flux.

twist.text: At night, with no solar input, the surface cools rapidly—especially under clear skies with low humidity.

climax.text: Globally, the energy budget balances—but locally, imbalances drive winds, storms, and ocean currents.

punchline.text: Weather exists because the budget is never even everywhere.

quiz.question: What happens when Earth's local energy budget is imbalanced?
options: It drives weather and ocean currents
